propositions: The T10 rubric must add a scope clause distinguishing durable infrastructure from transient, throwaway de-risk experiments.

The rubric must immediately follow that scope clause with a safety qualifier retaining four MAJOR classes: destructive apply, wildcard-admin access, plaintext secrets, and untrusted-network endpoint authentication.
The T10 rubric must remain independent and not reference or delegate scope to other overlays (e.g., T15).
A packaged eval spec must provide ten dataset cases (five pass, five finding) covering routine transient lifecycle, durable safety, and preserved MAJOR-class violations.
Offline text-contract tests must lock the exact scope clause, exact co-located safety qualifier, and rubric independence.
Live criterion evaluation must confirm all ten cases pass or find as labeled across three runs with stable agreement.
